title: Bundles
description: One reproduction manifest per act. Generated by scripts/build_bundles.py, which assembles each bundle, RUNS ITS OWN SCRIPT, captures what it printed, writes the archive and then reads size, hash and contents back off the file it wrote. Consumed by components/bundle-panel in part 6 of each act, and on /start/, /log/method/ and any evidence record that has a bundle. Nothing here is asserted: a manifest whose hash disagrees with the artifact fails the build, and a bundle whose script does not run fails before a manifest exists.

route.description: The act this bundle belongs to. One panel per act, in part 6.

href.description: Site-absolute. The file is in public/ and ships with the build, so the link is checked by gate 10 like any other.

format.description: Part of the download link's accessible name, with the size, so a screen reader user knows what they are about to fetch.

contents.description: The archive's own name list, read back after writing it. Never a list somebody typed.

sizeBytes.description: The file on disk. Rendered in the largest sensible unit.

sha256.description: The file on disk. The archive is written with fixed timestamps and modes in sorted order, so two builds over unchanged inputs produce the same hash; without that a panel would advertise a different hash every build and nobody could check one. The full value is in the DOM and the display form is truncated.

commit.description: The site commit that generated the archive, full form, so the panel can link the repository at that ref and truncate for display.

command.description: What a reader runs. Rendered in the adjacent code-block, and the command CI runs before diffing its output against expectedOutput.

requirementsKey.description: The copy key carrying what a reader needs, named rather than copied. Requirements are prose and prose lives in copy.yaml; a generator composing this sentence would be inventing a string.

expectedOutput.description: STDOUT OF THE BUNDLE'S OWN SCRIPT, CAPTURED AT GENERATION TIME. A reproduction path with no stated expected result is not reproducible, and an expected result somebody typed rots into a description of what the script used to do. Missing fails the build naming the route.

reproducedBy.description: Null on every bundle, and null is the true value: copy.yaml:ui.not_reproduced reads "No independent reproduction recorded." and that is what the panel renders. It cannot be derived, because a reproduction is a fact about somebody else's machine, so it arrives as a reviewed change and never as something a build inferred. Not a badge, not a tick, not green, in either direction.
